title: DINO-Mix: Distilling Foundational Knowledge with Cross-Domain CutMix for Semi-supervised Class-imbalanced Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: A frozen DINOv3 serves as an external, unbiased teacher for minority classes, which breaks the confirmation bias of inward-looking SSL. Progressive imbalance-aware CutMix forces attention to minority classes in labelled and unlabelled data.
adaptation: Minority classes = inactive, splice, gridline, edge_dark. Imbalance-aware CutMix pastes inactive regions, with their bordering cracks, into pool and train cells. DINOv3 feature similarity guides the rare classes.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + imbalance-aware CutMix + DINOv3 rare-class distillation, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metrics: inactive IoU (clean 49, BMRK subset, E1), gridline and splice IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill: inactive IoU < PF + 0.03 and mIoU_rob < PF + 0.01.
evidence: R: Synapse at 20% labels, 66.45 Dice vs 64.27 (SKCDF). AMOS at 5% labels, 62.73 vs 53.81. Low-label settings only.
prior_overlap: Partial. SKCDF-style heads were tested at 5% (worse or n.d.), and crack copy-paste onto pool cells was n.d. Inactive-focused CutMix with a DINOv3 teacher at 100% labels is untested.
